answer:
The author of *Lectures on Jurisprudence* is **Adam Smith** (1723–1790), the Scottish philosopher and economist. Several prestigious prizes bear his name; however, the most renowned academic award—the **Adam Smith Prize**—is granted by the **Faculty of Economics at the University of Cambridge**. This prize is awarded annually for the best overall examination performance and best dissertation in Part IIB of the Economics Tripos.

Other notable awards named after Adam Smith include:  
- **National Association of Business Economists (NABE) Adam Smith Award**: Honors leadership in business economics.  
- **Association of Private Enterprise Education (APEE) Adam Smith Award**: Recognizes contributions to free-market ideals.  
- **Panmure House Prize**: Administered jointly by Heriot-Watt University and FCLTGlobal, honoring research into long-term funding innovation.  
- **Royal Society of Edinburgh (RSE) Adam Smith Medal**: Acknowledges exceptional achievement by Scottish-connected researchers in business or public service.  

When referencing a single prominent institution associated with this honor, the **University of Cambridge** is the primary administrator of the canonical Adam Smith Prize.
